title: Attention Mechanisms for Social Engagements of Robots with Multiple People

fields.value: Technical/system description with an implemented robot system and experimental demonstration.

quotes.text: This paper first describes a multiple agent-based architecture designed to support HRI and then introduces an engagement mechanism based on attention distraction.

A Pioneer 3-AT mobile robot (called TourMate) was used to validate our social interaction mechanism based on attention/distraction within the HRI framework that was previously developed as described in [2].
A demonstration of interaction from solitude to active engagement was provided.

fields.value: Demonstration in the second floor of Torrence Hall at Tennessee State University; the described setup includes a robot home position and a remote microphone/computer at a known goal location.

The purpose of this paper is to present an attention/distraction mechanism within a framework for effective HRI on a mobile robot.

fields.value: An autonomous multi-agent HRI system uses face detection, sound-source localization, and speech recognition to generate decaying, per-person attention signals; these are combined and evaluated against thresholds. An emergency keyword overrides ordinary attention. The robot also uses speech output, information filtering, and navigation.

quotes.text: Face detection and sound source localization systems independently monitor the environment for detecting the presence of humans. Whenever a person is detected, an event is raised and a decaying attention signal is generated.

The speech recognition system generates context- and dependent levels of decaying attention signals. If the robot's perception is that the person is speaking directly to it, the attention signal generated has a higher coefficient compared to when the speech is not directed to the robot.

When Attk (n) is above a certain lower-threshold value, the robot is considered as occupied and its attention is not distracted unless the signal generated by another person Attj (n) is above an upper-threshold.
The speech library contains a keyword "Emergency" that acts as an emergency attention-getter.

fields.value: Pioneer 3-AT mobile robot platform, called TourMate, equipped with SLAM and navigation capabilities.

quotes.text: The system developed at Tennessee State University (TSU) on a Pioneer 3-AT mobile robot platform (TourMate) produced by ActivMedia (Fig. 1).
TourMate is equipped with Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) and Navigational capabilities.

fields.value: The paper presents a mobile robot system that combines face, sound, and speech inputs into decaying attention signals to manage engagement with multiple people. In its demonstration, the robot ignored a second person's greeting while engaged with the first, then tried to engage the second person after the first interaction waned.

RQ1; RQ2; RQ4; RQ5 — The paper frames attention as modality-based, decaying signals and describes its role in selecting and maintaining engagement among multiple people. It details the sensing, signal combination, thresholds, and robot platform; it does not study gaze behavior or report effects of embodiment.
